name: Filler Background Text Animation
use_when: A short-form talking-head section needs a quick visual reset without complex B-roll.
The spoken point can be carried by a short centered text phrase.
The edit needs a light body pattern break after the hook.
An editorial explainer needs a simple serif text card over a warm paper/grid background.
A tutorial, essay, countdown, or tips video needs a full-screen chapter card or section reset.
avoid_when: The line needs proof, footage, or a real object rather than text on a background.
The frame already has captions or overlays that make another text layer cluttered.
The subject tone would make a graphic card feel cheap or evasive.
A small label would be faster than a full-screen scene change.

timeline_pattern.pattern: spoken_phrase -> lift_text_layer -> add_flat_or_gradient_background -> center_text -> vary_weight_or_style -> clear_back_to_footage
timeline_pattern.contrast_rule: Pair light backgrounds with dark text and colored backgrounds with high-contrast text.
timeline_pattern.variation_rule: Use bold, italic, or weight changes only for meaning-changing words.
timeline_pattern.duration_rule: Keep the card onscreen only while the phrase is useful.
timeline_pattern.editorial_rule: For documentary graphics, pair serif title text with restrained labels, warm paper texture, and a limited accent palette.
timeline_pattern.chapter_card_rule: For section resets, animate the background card in first, then the short title, hold briefly, and animate both out before returning to footage.

motion.rule: Simple centered text and a clean background are enough; optional pop or zoom should not fight readability.

keyframe_values.text_position: Center text when the background replaces the talking head and no proof object needs priority.
keyframe_values.gradient: Use two to four compatible colors with enough contrast against the text.
keyframe_values.entrance: If animated, keep entrance around 4-8 frames for high-energy social style.
keyframe_values.editorial_intro: For editorial intros, stagger text and labels in reading order, then compound and trim the finished animation.
keyframe_values.section_card_canvas: Design imported backgrounds at the delivery ratio, such as 1920x1080 for horizontal or 1080x1920 for vertical.

sound.rule: Use no SFX or a very light pop; do not make every filler card a major transition.

captions.rule: Remove duplicate subtitles if the centered text already carries the spoken phrase clearly.

color.rule: Use background colors that match the short's style pack while preserving text contrast.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create a color source or gradient background, draw centered text, and trim the card to the spoken phrase.
implementation.remotion: Use a BackgroundTextCard component with text, backgroundType, colors, emphasisWords, startFrame, and duration.
implementation.blender: Use a flat plane or world background with text objects for more dimensional style packs.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add a canvas/background color, imported card, paper/grid background or gradient, center text, and apply minimal slide/pop/wipe/opacity motion if needed.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Color Matte or Four-Color Gradient under Essential Graphics text; copy/paste Motion position across text layers for consistency.

common_mistakes: Using filler cards when B-roll or proof would communicate better.
Leaving ordinary captions on top of the same centered phrase.
Overusing filler cards until the body feels like a slideshow.
Adding style variation to random words rather than meaning-changing words.
Using another publisher's exact logo/title identity instead of a project-specific editorial variant.
Using a full-screen card so often that every section reset feels slow.
qc: The text card has a clear story or pacing job.
Text is readable at phone size over the chosen background.
Duplicate captions are removed or simplified.
The card clears before it slows the next spoken concept.
Color and weight changes emphasize meaningful words only.
Any editorial text card uses licensed/project-owned logos and does not copy protected identity.
If the card is a chapter reset, do text and background clear before the next body beat?
